book_profile.narrator_stance: close, warm, theatrical — full expressive range, big swings encouraged

scenes.description: Ava consistently treats an ordinary rescued duckling as Egyptian royalty — 'Pharaoh Duckie,' 'His Majesty,' 'Duck King,' the 'palace lawn,' a 'royal basket,' and a 'court' of neighbor kids. The humor comes from the mismatch between grand, ceremonial language and a tiny mundane hatchling. Deliver these lines with mock-regal grandeur and proclamation cadence throughout; the payoff is Mama's deadpan 'You're funny,' where the reader briefly steps outside the game before Ava returns to it.

Mama's early worry that the duckling 'might be germy' quietly pays off at the end when, after cuddles, 'they wash their hands very well.' This is dual-audience deadpan humor: the child hears a tidy routine, the adult reader catches the callback to the germ warning. Deliver the handwashing line with a knowing, understated lilt rather than as a throwaway.

The genuine emotional spine of the story: Ava insists they must save the trapped duckling, bonds with him all day, then must let him go to the humane society despite wanting to keep him — resolved two months later when she believes she sees him flying free to the lake. Real stakes and emotion, not a joke. Build warmth and urgency at the start, land the tearful low point when Ava must give him up, and finish with tender, hopeful wonder.

Throughout the first half, Mama is on the phone arranging the duck's rescue while Ava plays. These phone fragments are parallel background action and should stay audio-subordinate — quieter, slightly turned-away, muffled — so they never compete with Ava's foreground royal play.

chunks.text: Meep Meep Meep. Meep Meep Meep.
chunks.speaker: Duckling
chunks.note: Opening onomatopoeia — the whole chunk is the sound itself; likely a duckling/bird chirp that sets up Ava's discovery. Speaker guessed from context.

chunks.text: “Mama, Mama, come quick.” Ava tugs at the back of her mom’s gardening shirt.
chunks.speaker: Ava
chunks.note: Child urgently calling for mom to come see something — insistent tugging, breathless energy rather than fear.

chunks.text: Mama stands and squints. “What is it this time, nature girl?”
chunks.speaker: Mama
chunks.note: Affectionate, slightly amused tone — 'nature girl' is a warm teasing nickname suggesting this happens often

chunks.text: Meep Meep Meep
chunks.speaker: Baby duck (duckling)
chunks.note: The trapped duckling's peeping — small, high, distressed cheeps; delivered as the sound itself, not narration.

chunks.text: “A baby duck is trapped in the window hole,” Ava shouts. “We have to save him.”
chunks.speaker: Ava
chunks.note: Text says 'shouts' — urgent plea to rescue the trapped duckling; worry rides under the excited urgency.

chunks.text: “Don’t touch that duckling, honey. It might be germy. Let me call someone,” Mama says.
chunks.speaker: Mama
chunks.note: Sets up the germy-duck handwashing callback; 'germy' is the seed word that pays off later, give it a light knowing stress. Mama is reassuring but mildly cautious.

chunks.text: And just like that, she’s on the phone.
chunks.note: Light narrator aside with a hint of wry timing — Mom springs into action instantly; 'just like that' carries a small amused beat.

chunks.text: “...no, it’s a feral duck,” Mom says on the phone in the background.
chunks.speaker: Mom
chunks.note: Overheard background phone chatter — keep it offhand and quieter than the main dialogue to read as ambient.

chunks.text: “Come here, Pharaoh Duckie, or you are going to cook in this sun.”
chunks.speaker: Ava
chunks.note: Ava coaxing the duck with an affectionate, playful royal name — part of the royal-duck-naming motif setup; warm and cajoling rather than urgent.

chunks.text: Ava follows her fluffy Egyptian king all over the palace lawn.
chunks.note: Part of the royal-duck-naming motif: mundane duckling described in grand royal terms ('Egyptian king','palace lawn') — deliver with whimsical mock-grandeur to land the incongruity.

chunks.text: “You have a Waterfowl Center?” Mom asks into her phone
chunks.speaker: Mom

illustration_inference.implied_scene: Mom stands on the sunny palace lawn holding her phone to her ear with a bemused, eyebrow-raised expression, glancing toward Ava and the fluffy duckling waddling nearby.

chunks.note: Background phone conversation; questioning inflection, casual not high-stakes

chunks.text: Ava gently places His Majesty in a royal basket.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: Ava, kneeling on the palace lawn, carefully lowers a fluffy yellow duckling into a small basket lined like a throne, her face tender and focused while Mom stands nearby distracted on her phone.

chunks.note: Royal-naming motif (build): 'His Majesty' and 'royal basket' get an affectionate, mock-ceremonial lilt over an ordinary duckling in a basket; 'gently' cues soft, warm delivery

chunks.text: Ava wonders if the royal duck knows how to swim yet. She decides to give him a lesson. Ava fills up her water table with the garden hose.
chunks.note: Ava's gentle caretaking curiosity; the 'royal duck' framing carries playful warmth. Lean slightly above the flat prose per the illustrated-spread energy.

chunks.text: “...great, yes, we will be here…Mom says, still on the phone.
chunks.speaker: Mom
chunks.note: Background phone chatter, half-distracted and casual — trailing off, not directed at Ava.

chunks.text: The neighbor kids stop by. Every Pharaoh needs a court.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: A cluster of neighborhood kids gather at the fence and yard around Ava and her water table, being playfully recruited into the duck's royal court as Ava assigns them roles.

chunks.note: Incongruity humor: an ordinary duckling treated as royalty. The deadpan 'Every Pharaoh needs a court' lands the joke — a slight knowing lilt, not a flat read.

chunks.text: “His Majesty, the Duck King, has learned how to swim,” Ava pronounces.
chunks.speaker: Ava
chunks.note: Mock-royal proclamation — grand, ceremonious delivery over the mundane fact of swimming; incongruity is the joke. Part of the royal-naming motif.

chunks.text: Ava lays out a picnic blanket in a shady spot and places a birdseed treat on top.
chunks.note: Sparse action line but part of the whimsical royal-court make-believe; keep a light playful energy.

chunks.text: “Pharaoh Duck will take his picnic in the garden this sunny day,” Ava proclaims.
chunks.speaker: Ava
chunks.note: Part of royal-naming-motif: mundane duckling given grand royal treatment. Deliver with mock-regal proclamation flourish for the incongruity humor.

chunks.text: The court entertains their Duck King.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: On the shady picnic blanket, Ava and a few smaller creatures (a cat, toys, or bugs) bow, dance, and perform for a plump duck perched grandly on a cushion like a tiny throne.

chunks.note: Sparse line for a full illustrated ceremonial spread — the royal-duck motif is mock-grand play; lean into whimsical mock-regal energy rather than flat narration.

chunks.text: The court promenades with their Duck King.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: Ava and her friends parade in a stately line across the sunny garden lawn, holding the duck aloft on a cushion or in a decorated basket like royalty in procession.

chunks.note: Part of the royal-duck-naming motif — the grand word 'promenades' applied to kids parading a duckling is gentle incongruity humor; sparse line should be delivered with mock-ceremonial whimsy.

chunks.text: The court keeps their Duck King safe.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: A cluster of children huddle protectively around a small duck perched on a cushion or in cupped hands, shielding him with outstretched arms from wind or a curious dog on the lawn.

chunks.note: Part of the royal-naming-motif build; sparse picture-book line carrying warmth of children protecting their pretend Duck King — lean into the affectionate 'court' conceit.

chunks.text: The court has to go home for dinner.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: At dusk, the group of children (the 'court') trudge reluctantly away across the lawn toward home, glancing back over their shoulders at the little duckling left behind on the grass, as a parent calls them in for dinner.

chunks.note: Gentle turn toward the story winding down; slight wistfulness as playtime ends, but stays in warm narrator register.

chunks.text: Even royals need a cuddle.
chunks.note: Playful royal-naming motif meets a genuinely warm, affectionate beat — gentle and intimate, with a light comedic lilt on the incongruity of royalty needing a cuddle.

chunks.text: “Ava, bring the duckling, the humane society is here,” Mama says.
chunks.speaker: Mama
chunks.note: Gentle parental instruction; leads into the emotional release-of-the-duckling beat that follows.

chunks.text: “Aww Mama, can’t we keep him?” Tears creep into Ava’s eyes.
chunks.speaker: Ava
chunks.note: Child pleading to keep the duckling while genuinely tearing up — pleading protest riding over real sadness; keep quiet but emotionally high, don't average to medium.

chunks.text: “No, baby.” Mama smiles down at the fluffy, little hatchling. “He needs time to grow and a safe place to do it.”
chunks.speaker: Mama
chunks.note: Gentle, comforting refusal — Mama softening the disappointment for Ava while explaining kindly.

chunks.text: Ava wipes her tears. “But His Majesty was just about to have his bubble bath.”
chunks.note: Ava pivots from tears into a negotiating plea, dressing up the duckling as royalty (build of the royal-naming motif) — the mock-grand 'His Majesty' should carry a playful, coaxing lilt over lingering upset.

chunks.text: “His Majesty?” Mama says. “You’re funny.”
chunks.speaker: Mama

illustration_inference.implied_scene: Mama crouches at Ava's level, laughing warmly with a hand on her shoulder, while Ava clutches the tiny fluffy duckling protectively between them in a cozy home setting.

chunks.note: Payoff of the royal-duck-naming motif — Mama is gently amused by Ava's over-the-top 'His Majesty'; warm, affectionate teasing rather than mockery

chunks.text: “Are you sure he will be okay?”
chunks.speaker: Ava
chunks.note: Child seeking reassurance about the duck she loves — worry with underlying affection

chunks.text: Mama gives Ava and Pharaoh Duck a quick cuddle too.

illustration_inference.implied_scene: Mama kneels down and wraps her arms around Ava, who is clutching a small toy or rubber duck ('Pharaoh Duck'), pulling both child and duck into a warm quick embrace with tender smiles.

chunks.note: Warm affectionate beat as Mama cuddles both child and duck; gentle delivery.

chunks.text: Then they wash their hands very well.
chunks.note: Dry/ironic callback payoff to the germy-duck handwashing motif — deliver deadpan, understated; the humor lands for the adult reading aloud. Resist over-playing it.

chunks.text: “The High Society will transport you to your castle now, Your Majesty,” Ava whispers to Pharaoh Duck.
chunks.note: Callback to the royal-duck-naming motif — grand ceremonial language ('High Society','your castle','Your Majesty') applied tenderly to a pet duck; whispered but affectionate, keep the mock-regal charm warm.

chunks.text: And they do.
chunks.note: Sparse resolution line paying off the release; the short sentence carries the warm satisfaction of the whole save-and-release arc, so lean gentle and heartfelt rather than flat.

chunks.text: …Two months later Ava is sure she sees her Pharaoh Duck flying overhead to his palace by the lake.
chunks.note: Closing line of the book — warm, wistful resolution of the save-and-release arc plus a gentle callback to the royal-duck naming. The leading ellipsis and 'is sure she sees' invite a soft, dreamy, hopeful delivery.
